resolution: Stage one failed 5/7: hipOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor did not reproduce the two odd-WGP counter cases. The gfx942 row is therefore an observation of the runtime API, not evidence for either hardware granule hypothesis.
gate_wording_correction: The registered claim said blocks_per_multiprocessor should reproduce waves_per_CU and equal workgroups_per_WGP. Those are different units: one 64-thread RDNA block is two wave32 waves. The resolved gate uses the probe's already-emitted waves_per_multiprocessor. No prediction, threshold or row was changed; results/hip_occupancy_probe_result.json preserves the original wording and the dimensional correction.
question: Does the occupancy model describe a mechanism, or does it fit seven RDNA footprints?
why_this_can_be_asked_now: The model is about LDS bytes, a rounding granule and a pool division. It says nothing about matrix instructions, so a probe that allocates shared memory and does nothing else can carry it to another architecture. hip/fused_peps_kernel.hip cannot: every WMMA builtin in it is _w32 and needs gfx11-insts, which CDNA does not have.

model.pool_scope_rdna: per workgroup processor, which is two compute units
model.fitted_on: seven gfx1151 footprints, confirmed on an eighth chosen to break it

probe.known_limit: The probe sweeps dynamic shared memory; the committed counter measurements used static __shared__. Agreement on the seven RDNA footprints is what would show the two are accounted the same way. Without that agreement nothing here transfers.
probe.not_a_counter: This is the runtime's own occupancy calculation, not a hardware counter. It is admissible as an oracle only if it reproduces the counter measurements on the part where both exist, which is what test one asks.

test_one_is_the_oracle_admissible.run_on: gfx1201, and gfx1151 if it is reachable
test_one_is_the_oracle_admissible.claim: blocks_per_multiprocessor reproduces the committed waves_per_cu on all seven footprints
test_one_is_the_oracle_admissible.passes_if: each row equals the workgroups_per_wgp column below
test_one_is_the_oracle_admissible.and_settles: whether HIP counts a workgroup processor or a compute unit as a multiprocessor. This repository already read multiProcessorCount as a compute-unit count and was wrong by a factor of two, so the two readings are written out separately rather than assumed.
test_one_is_the_oracle_admissible.fails_if: the values land on if_multiprocessor_means_cu instead, which would mean the API and the counters disagree about the unit and the oracle cannot be carried to CDNA without resolving that first

constants_that_change.pool_scope: per compute unit; CDNA has no workgroup processor
constants_that_change.waves_per_block: one, because a 64-thread block is a single wave64

test_two_does_the_form_survive_a_change_.claim: the form survives with CDNA's own constants: blocks per compute unit equals floor(65536 / effective)

the_decisive_footprint.why: 10752 is the only footprint in the sweep where the two granules disagree; 10752 is exactly 84 x 128, so a 128-byte granule leaves it alone while a 1024-byte granule rounds it to 11264. Every other footprint gives the same answer either way and therefore tests nothing.

test_two_does_the_form_survive_a_change_.what_a_failure_would_mean: That the 1024-byte granule is an RDNA fact rather than a general one. That is a result, not a setback: the model would still hold where it was measured, and its scope would be known rather than assumed.

limitations: This file preserves the preregistered predictions. Measurements live in results/hip_occupancy_probe_result.json and the three raw receipts it names; none of the prediction rows was rewritten after the run.
The CDNA host is a single-GPU container slice with no profiler, so the counter cross-check that was available on gfx1151 is not available there. Stage one rejected the runtime API as a substitute.

Occupancy may be bounded by registers or wave slots rather than LDS at the smaller footprints. The observed mismatch was checked against the preregistered gate and rejects this API as an oracle; it does not rewrite the counter model.
